answer: An agent economy can make each identity a custodian of randomly assigned data shards, stored like the petals of a lotus: every epoch, the network asks for a random shard, and only an identity that truly stores it can answer in time. A Sybil farmer running a hundred puppets on one disk cannot hold a separate vault of data for each puppet, so each fake identity must buy real storage or fail the check, and one missed retrieval marks it for audit. The cost scales with the number of puppets, while an honest agent pays only for its own violet shard.
